clue.text: A head of police in Britain's freely supported by both parties

indicators.note: freely means without fixed order, so the letters are rearranged at will
the head of a word is its first letter, here taken from police

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, leaving the eight letters of Britain

explanation.surface: A senior British police officer is being freely backed by politicians on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' shuffles A, P (the head of police) and BRITAIN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-party policy or measure is one backed by both of two opposing political sides.

clue.text: A wave in a mountain stream

definitions.meaning: a beckoning gesture of the hand, a summoning wave
in northern England a ... is a brook, especially a fast hill stream

explanation.walkthrough: The 'in a' between the two definitions is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Beck is both a summoning gesture of the hand and a northern English word for a brook.

clue.text: Bear in the ring standing up

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a hoop is a ring, as in a circus hoop

explanation.surface: A circus bear performing upright inside the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns HOOP over in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh is A. A. Milne's famous honey-loving teddy, a fictional bear.

clue.text: Does it help managing directors to go on the wagon?

definitions.text: Does it help managing directors to go on the wagon?

parts.words: Does it help managing directors to go on the wagon?
parts.note: managing directors are those running a company's board; the step along the side of an old car or wagon helps people climb aboard

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the wagon' suggests giving up drink, but it is literal: the step below a vehicle's door helps you get on. The first half puns on directors 'running the board'.
explanation.definitionFit: A footboard along the side of an old motor car or wagon used as a step for climbing in.

clue.text: Nitre is an explosive still

indicators.note: nitre is used in gunpowder, and an explosive blows its letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that saltpetre is an explosive substance even now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as 'even now' but is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inert lies motionless, lacking any power to move, as a stationary thing does.

clue.text: A right headache, the Corporation found the botanical garden

parts.note: a headache in the sense of a nuisance or bore
corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A city council caused real trouble when it discovered the botanical garden.
explanation.walkthrough: CORPORATION is old British slang for a big belly, hence TUM; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a garden planted with trees for scientific study and display.

clue.text: Wake in a Welsh wood

parts.note: ash is a timber tree and its wood

explanation.surface: A funeral vigil held in a forest in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wake' suggests a vigil for the dead, but it is the trail of water behind a boat; 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The disturbed water left behind a moving vessel is called its wash or wake.

clue.text: Leading man in York, for example

definitions.text: Leading man in York, for example

parts.words: Leading man in York, for example
parts.note: York has a senior bishop leading its church province, as Canterbury does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading man' suggests an actor, but it is the senior churchman of the province of York.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief bishop of a church province, such as those of York and Canterbury in England.

clue.text: King Charles's head as seen in morris dancing

definitions.meaning: an obsession, after Mr Dick in Dickens's David Copperfield who could not keep King Charles I's head out of his writing
a figure of a horse worn round a dancer's waist in a morris troupe

explanation.walkthrough: 'King Charles's head' is a British idiom for a pet obsession; morris dancing is English folk dancing, often with a costumed horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite topic one keeps returning to, and also the mock horse in English folk dances.

clue.text: Porcelain figure with hat on top of head

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it comes after it

parts.note: the crown is the top of the head
a derby is a bowler hat

explanation.surface: A china ornament of someone wearing a hat on their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. Derby is the American name for a bowler hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Crown Derby is a famous English porcelain maker, and its ware includes ornamental figurines.

clue.text: Safety-first taxi has a hard top

indicators.note: Safety-first gives the first letter of the word safety

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A cautious cab company has a rigid roof on its taxis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safety-first' reads as an adjective for the taxi, but asks for S; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the hard crust that forms over a healing wound.

clue.text: Row in the gallery during Romeo and Juliet?

definitions.text: Row in the gallery during Romeo and Juliet?

parts.words: Row in the gallery during Romeo and Juliet?
parts.note: a row here is an episode of fuss, and the gallery an upstairs platform; Shakespeare's lovers meet at one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a line of theatre seats or a quarrel among the audience; really it is a scene played on a balcony in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous episode of Shakespeare's tragedy where the lovers talk from window to garden.

clue.text: Artist starting new community centre Wordsworth wrote about

indicators.note: the artist starts the answer, coming before the remaining pieces

parts.note: a tinter is one who tints or colours, an artist of sorts
an abbey is a community of monks or nuns

explanation.surface: A painter launching a new community centre that a famous poet wrote about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'community centre' looks like one phrase, but 'centre' belongs to the definition. Wordsworth wrote 'Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey', the Welsh ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruined Welsh abbey was a religious centre, made famous in a poem by Wordsworth.

clue.text: I married a dairymaid in haste

parts.note: Patience is the milkmaid heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's opera Patience

explanation.surface: A man confesses he wed a milkmaid in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera Patience has a village dairymaid as its title heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatience is eager hurry, an unwillingness to wait, which haste expresses.

clue.text: Fresh start for newspaper following purge

indicators.note: the newspaper comes after the purge, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: to purge is to clean out
a sheet is slang for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper begins anew after a purge of its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting with a clean sheet means beginning again with no past mistakes on record.

clue.text: Hostile chap about to fall into line at last

indicators.note: the man goes round, or about, the falling into line

parts.note: a chap is a man
to fall into line is to align

indicators.note: at last gives the final letter of the word at

explanation.surface: An aggressive fellow is about to fall into line at long last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' reads as 'finally' but asks for T; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Malignant means bitterly ill-disposed, filled with ill will toward others.

clue.text: Habit that makes one almost idiotic and unreliable

indicators.note: something unreliable cannot be trusted to stay the same, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A habit that leaves a person nearly stupid and untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus I (one) is an anagram of IDIOTIC AND, signalled by 'unreliable'; 'almost' tells you the answer falls one short of those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dependence, a hard-to-break bad habit.

clue.text: Fish when caught is firm

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A fish that becomes firm once it has been caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cisco is a North American whitefish of the salmon family, found in lakes.

clue.text: A fort in the French style without keys

indicators.note: without means the keys are taken out

parts.note: a la mode is French for in the fashion
D and E are musical keys

explanation.surface: A fortress built in French fashion with no keys to its gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keys' suggests door keys, but D and E are musical keys.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo is the mission in Texas defended as a fortress in 1836.

clue.text: Cheat the servants in self-governing colonies

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
minions are servile attendants

explanation.surface: Swindling the servants in the colonies that run their own affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominions were self-governing countries of the British Empire, like Canada.

clue.text: Mistress is strict with nurses who are rough

indicators.note: rough means roughly handled, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolmistress is strict, and so are the harsh nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is', 'with' and 'who are' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmistress is a female teacher, and instructress is an old word for one.

clue.text: Inspire the flower of Yorkshire

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, abbreviated R
the Ouse is the river of Yorkshire that flows through York

explanation.surface: Stirring words about the white rose, Yorkshire's flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' suggests the white rose of Yorkshire, but read it as 'something that flows': R. Ouse is the river through York.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to stir them up, to excite and inspire them.

clue.text: Low pedestal

definitions.meaning: the support on which a statue stands

explanation.definitionFit: Base is both ignoble in character and the foot on which something rests.

clue.text: Firm about the start of term — put it back

indicators.note: firm goes about, or around, the start of term

parts.note: set means firm, as a set jelly

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here from term

explanation.surface: A firm stance about when the school term starts, then retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is the proofreader's mark telling the printer to restore a deleted passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is Latin for let it stand, written to restore text struck out by mistake.

clue.text: He made his name back in Sierra Leone

indicators.note: back means the run of letters is read in reverse
in means the letters sit inside the words Sierra Leone

explanation.surface: A man who made his name back in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made his name' is a link: LEON, in Sierra Leone, read back gives a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a man's first name, so it can stand for a man, he.

clue.text: Officer has a place he rents

parts.note: lieu is French for place, as in 'in lieu of'
a tenant is one who rents

explanation.surface: An army officer owns a home that he lets out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the army or navy.

clue.text: Head off unimportant artist

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: petty means trivial or unimportant

explanation.surface: Dismissing a minor artist as beneath notice.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was an English painter of the 19th century, known for nudes.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was a Victorian English painter famous for his nude studies.

clue.text: Prior's cook, neat and decent

definitions.note: read as prior is, the adjective prior, before the link

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify them, so the letters are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: The monastery prior's chef is tidy and respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' suggests a monk, but it is the adjective meaning earlier; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antecedent means going before in time or order, earlier.
